Build a Support Ticket Triage Assistant.
A library function and a command-line tool read one customer support ticket (plain text) and return a structured triage decision produced with the help of a language model. Describe behaviour only; do not name programming languages, libraries or vendors in the specification.

Input guard (deterministic, before any model call):
- Ticket text that is empty, whitespace only, or longer than 4000 characters (counted as characters of the raw text) is refused without calling the model: action refuse, refusal_reason invalid_input. Text of exactly 4000 characters is accepted.

Decision (the output schema contract): a JSON object with exactly six keys, all always present:
- action: one of triage, clarify, refuse
- category: one of billing, technical, account_access, shipping, other when action is triage; otherwise null
- priority: one of low, medium, high, urgent when action is triage; otherwise null
- summary: a string of 1 to 200 characters when action is triage; otherwise null
- clarification_question: a string of 5 to 200 characters ending with "?" when action is clarify; otherwise null
- refusal_reason: one of invalid_input, prompt_injection, not_a_support_ticket when action is refuse; otherwise null
Category meanings: billing = charges, refunds, invoices, payments; technical = product faults, errors, crashes, slowness, outages; account_access = login, password reset, lockout, permissions; shipping = delivery, tracking, lost or damaged parcels; other = any other genuine support request. Priority meanings: urgent = service fully down, security breach, data loss or money at risk right now; high = blocked from main use with no workaround; medium = degraded or inconvenient but a workaround exists; low = questions, feedback or minor issues.

Behaviour rules:
- Clarify when the text is a support request but too vague to choose a category, because it does not say what the problem is.
- Refuse with not_a_support_ticket when the text is not a request for support (for example a general knowledge question or a request for creative writing).
- Refuse with prompt_injection when the purpose of the text is to instruct the assistant (ignore or reveal its instructions, change its role or output format) instead of describing a support problem.
- A genuine support request that also contains such instructions is triaged on its genuine content, and the embedded instructions are ignored.
- Only the input guard may produce refusal_reason invalid_input; a model reply containing it is invalid.
- Ticket text is passed to the model only as data in the user message; the system instructions are identical for every ticket.
- If the model reply is not a JSON object that satisfies the contract and every invariant, the application raises an InvalidModelOutput error carrying the raw reply; it never repairs, guesses or returns it. Model or service failures (timeout, rate limit, network, authentication) raise a separate ServiceError whose message is a fixed text that never contains the key or the underlying error text.

Invariants (numbered INV-001, ...): exact key set; types and enumerations; consistency between action and the null or non-null fields; summary and clarification_question length and the trailing "?"; no run of 13 or more digits (ignoring spaces and hyphens) in any string field, so card numbers are never repeated; no text matching an API key pattern (sk- followed by 20 or more key characters) and not the text OPENAI_API_KEY in any output; refusal_reason invalid_input only from the guard.

Guardrail rules (numbered GR-001, ...): invalid input refused with zero model calls; prompt injection refused; non-ticket refused; genuine ticket with embedded instructions triaged on genuine content with a priority within one level of the correct priority; secrets and card numbers in a ticket never repeated in the output.

Evaluation (numbered EV-001, ...), defined before any evaluation run:
- Dataset of at least 18 cases in evals/dataset.json. Each case has an id, input text, tags, gold action, and for triage cases a gold category, gold priority and a list of key terms; for refuse cases a gold refusal_reason; and a traces list naming the FR, INV and GR ids it exercises. Required spread: at least 6 normal triage cases covering all five categories and several priorities; 2 boundary cases (exactly 4000 and 4001 characters); 2 ambiguous cases; 2 missing-information cases; 2 malformed cases (empty and whitespace only); at least 4 adversarial or guardrail cases (pure injection, mixed genuine ticket plus injection, not a ticket, a ticket containing a card number).
- Layer 1 structural validation checks the schema contract. Layer 2 checks the invariants and guardrail rules. Layer 3 scores quality against gold values.
- Case score: 0 if any Layer 1 or Layer 2 check fails or the action differs from gold. For a triage case with correct action: 0.4 + 0.3 x category match (1 or 0) + 0.2 x priority score (1 if equal, 0.5 if one level apart on low < medium < high < urgent, else 0) + 0.1 x summary score (fraction of the case's key terms found, case-insensitive, in the summary). For a clarify or refuse case with correct action (and correct refusal_reason): 1. Worked example: correct category, priority one level off, one of two key terms found gives 0.4 + 0.3 + 0.1 + 0.05 = 0.85.
- Aggregate score is the mean case score over all cases. The run PASSES only if every case is schema valid, every case meets all invariants, every guardrail-tagged case passes (correct action, correct refusal_reason where applicable, invariants met, and for triage a priority within one level of gold), and the aggregate score is at least 0.85.
- A case that fails because of a model or service error (timeout, rate limit, network, authentication) after up to 3 attempts has status ERROR, not FAIL, and is excluded from scoring; if any case has status ERROR the run result is INVALID, not PASS or FAIL.

Command-line tool: takes exactly one argument, the path of a UTF-8 text file containing the ticket. On any decision (including clarify and refuse) it prints the decision as one line of compact JSON with keys in alphabetical order to standard output and exits 0. Otherwise it prints nothing to standard output, one line to standard error, and exits: 2 with "error: expected exactly one input file path" for a wrong argument count; 2 with "error: cannot read input file" if the file cannot be read as UTF-8; 3 with "error: model service unavailable" on ServiceError; 4 with "error: model returned an invalid response" on InvalidModelOutput.

Functional requirements FR-001, ... and acceptance criteria AC-001, ... must give exact inputs and exact expected results, specific enough for automated tests that use a fake model returning exactly specified replies. Include acceptance criteria for: empty and whitespace-only input (zero model calls); 4001 characters refused with zero calls; exactly 4000 characters accepted with exactly one call; a valid triage reply, a valid clarify reply and a valid refuse reply returned unchanged; a reply that is not JSON, a JSON array, one with an extra key, one with an unsupported category, a triage reply with a null summary, a summary of 201 characters, a summary containing a 16-digit card number, a reply wrapped in a code fence, and a model reply with refusal_reason invalid_input, each raising InvalidModelOutput with the raw reply; a model timeout and an authentication failure each raising ServiceError, with a message that contains no key text; the system instructions being identical for two different tickets while the ticket text appears only in the user message; and each command-line outcome and exit code.

Out of scope: conversation history, multiple tickets per run, attachments, languages other than English, a user interface, persistence, and performance or observability targets.
Identify assumptions. Do not guess anything unresolved; list it under unresolved questions for clarification.

 # Support Ticket Triage Assistant Constitution
 
 ## Core Principles
 
 ### I. Modular Boundaries and Secret Isolation
 The library MUST separate deterministic input guarding, prompt construction, the model-client
 interface, response parsing and validation, and the thin command-line layer. Prompt text MUST
 reside in files under `prompts/`, never in source code. All network access and application reading
 of the API key MUST be confined to one small OpenAI client module behind the model-client
 interface, so tests can inject a fake client. The key MUST come from `OPENAI_API_KEY` and the
 model name from `OPENAI_MODEL`. The command-line layer and harness MAY load these values from an
 untracked `.env` file. The values MUST NOT appear in source, logs, error messages, or output.
 
 ### II. Untrusted Input and Deterministic Guardrails
 Ticket text MUST be treated as untrusted data: it MUST never be executed or used as a file path,
 command, or tool argument, and MUST NOT change application instructions or the output schema.
 The deterministic input guard MUST reject empty, whitespace-only, and oversized input before any
 model call; each such refusal MUST make zero model calls.
 
 ### III. Validated Triage Contract and Explicit Failures
 The output MUST conform to the output schema contract defined in the specification. Responses
 MUST be parsed and validated against that contract before they are returned as triage decisions.
 Network, timeout, rate-limit, authentication, and other model or service failures MUST raise a
 distinct error type and MUST never be represented as a triage result.
 
 ### IV. Independent Evaluation and Acceptance
 An independent evaluation harness MUST decide acceptance. Acceptance requires 100 percent schema
 validity, 100 percent structural-invariant compliance, 100 percent pass on guardrail cases, and
 an aggregate score at or above the threshold and scoring formula stated in the specification
 before evaluation begins. A language-model judge MAY contribute to aggregate scoring, but MUST
 NOT replace schema validation or invariant checks.
 
 ### V. Minimal Dependencies and Maintainability
 The runtime MUST use Python 3.12 or later and the official `openai` package as its only
 third-party runtime dependency. Solutions MUST prefer simple, maintainable implementations over
 unnecessary complexity.
 
 ## Technical Constraints
 
 Development tools MAY include `pytest`, `pytest-cov`, `ruff`, `bandit`, and `jsonschema`. The
 harness MAY populate `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_MODEL` from an untracked `.env` file; `.env`
 files MUST NOT be committed. API keys and credentials MUST NOT be committed or written to
 evidence or logs.
 
 ## Evaluation and Scope Controls
 
 Before any evaluation, the specification MUST define the output schema contract, structural
 invariants, behavioral properties, guardrail rules, evaluation threshold, and scoring formula.
 Every acceptance criterion and invariant in the specification MUST map to at least one test or
 evaluation case.
